planting.note: Set out rooted seedlings or hardwood cuttings in spring into lean, sharply draining, rocky or gravelly soil in full sun; this tree tolerates near-total neglect once established but will not survive wet feet.

directions: Native to the limestone escarpments of Oman's Dhofar mountains and adjoining parts of Yemen and Somalia, this is the source tree of true frankincense, tapped by slashing the bark so the milky sap oozes out and hardens into fragrant amber-colored resin 'tears' that are collected, graded, and burned as incense or used in traditional medicine. Growth is extremely slow and the trunk often develops a swollen, papery-barked base adapted to surviving drought and poor, eroded soils where little else grows. Avoid rich garden soil, frequent watering, or any shade, all of which weaken the tree and reduce resin quality. Give it full sun and sharply draining, rocky ground, since it tolerates near-total neglect once established but will not survive wet feet.
sources: Kew Royal Botanic Gardens — Plants of the World Online
Purdue University Center for New Crops and Plant Products

planting.note: Root leafless hardwood stem cuttings in a gritty, fast-draining mix under warm, dry conditions, and only transplant into the garden once well rooted and frost danger has fully passed.

directions: Myrrh is a thorny, multi-stemmed desert shrub native to the dry Acacia-Commiphora bushland of Yemen and Oman's Dhofar region as well as Somalia and Ethiopia, where it has been tapped for its bitter, fragrant gum-resin for millennia as a companion commodity to frankincense along the ancient South Arabian incense trade routes. The resin hardens into reddish-brown lumps used historically in incense, perfume, and embalming, and still valued today in traditional medicine and aromatherapy. Keep the shrub in full baking sun with minimal irrigation and scrupulous drainage, since it rots quickly in cool, damp, or heavy soils. Root leafless hardwood stem cuttings under warm, dry conditions and only transplant once well established.
sources: Kew Royal Botanic Gardens — Plants of the World Online

planting.note: Transplant rooted cuttings into deep, well-drained soil on a sunny slope after frost danger has passed; plants are grown on terraced mountainsides and pruned hard to keep new, tender growth within easy picking reach.

directions: Native to the highlands of Yemen and the Horn of Africa, khat is cultivated for its young leaves and soft shoot tips, which are chewed fresh for their mild stimulant effect and form a deeply embedded cash crop across Yemen's terraced highland agriculture, particularly around Ibb, Taiz, and the Sana'a highlands. Growers harvest repeatedly through the year by hand-picking the newest leafy branch tips, which resprout readily after cutting, and the crop's year-round irrigation demand has made it a major factor in regional water-use debates. Left unpruned the shrub will grow into a small evergreen tree, but commercial plantings are kept coppiced low and bushy for easier harvest. Transplant rooted cuttings into deep, well-drained soil on a sunny slope after frost danger has passed.
sources: Kew Royal Botanic Gardens — Plants of the World Online

subcategory: Gulf syrup and processing date palm

planting.note: Plant rooted offshoots or tissue-cultured plantlets in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, giving each tree enough room for its mature crown spread.

directions: Mabsali is a long-established Omani cultivar grown widely across the Al Batinah coastal plain and interior oases, valued less as a table date than for its high sugar and moisture content, which makes it a preferred variety for boiling down into thick date syrup (dibs) and other processed date products, though it is also eaten locally at the soft khalal and rutab stages. Like other Gulf date cultivars it needs a long, intensely hot, dry summer to properly cure the ripening crop and depends on hand pollination or a nearby male pollinator to set fruit reliably. New offshoots generally need five to seven years of growth before reaching full commercial bearing. Plant rooted offshoots in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun with ample room for the mature crown spread.
sources: Sultan Qaboos University College of Agricultural and Marine Sciences

planting.note: Plant rooted offshoots or tissue-cultured plantlets in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, spacing trees widely to allow for their eventual crown spread.

directions: Umm-Sila is a traditional Omani cultivar grown through the Al Batinah plain and interior Dakhiliyah oases, prized chiefly as a fresh-eating date that is picked and sold at the soft, amber rutab stage rather than fully dried, in contrast to multi-purpose cultivars that are also cured hard for storage. It requires the same long, hot, dry summer that all Gulf dates need to ripen and sweeten properly, along with hand pollination or a nearby male tree to ensure a reliable fruit set. As with other named Omani cultivars, offshoots take roughly five to seven years to mature into full commercial production. Plant rooted offshoots in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, spacing trees widely for their eventual crown spread.
sources: Sultan Qaboos University College of Agricultural and Marine Sciences
